facts: DID develops as a response to repeated childhood trauma — it is a survival adaptation, not a flaw.
Alters (or 'parts') are not 'fake personalities.' Each one holds real feelings, memories, and roles.
People with DID are far more likely to be harmed than to harm anyone — the 'split-personality villain' is a myth.
Switching between alters is usually subtle, not the dramatic flip shown in movies.
Many systems experience 'co-consciousness,' where alters are aware of one another at the same time.
With support and therapy, people with DID can live full, stable, and meaningful lives.
Amnesia between parts exists on a spectrum and can lessen with healing.
The goal of therapy is usually cooperation between alters — not erasing them.
